description: Fairchild C-123 Provider; complete airframe; set on a bluff above Playa Manuel Antonio and converted into a restaurant; bar and coffee shop; the fuselage is the dining room and the wing shelters the bar terrace. Bought from San José Juan Santamaría in August 2000 for a reported USD 3;000; dismantled and barged around the coast to Quepos because it was too wide for the banana-railway bridges; and reassembled on site. Operator and press describe it as the surviving sister ship of the C-123K shot down over southern Nicaragua on 5 October 1986 (Corporate Air Services HPF821; ex-N4410F; c/n 20128; ex-USAF 54-679); the crash that exposed Iran-Contra when loadmaster Eugene Hasenfus was captured. A dated Flickr photograph of 12 July 2019 reads the serial painted on the airframe as USAF 54-663 and calls it a C-123B; that serial is from a single source and could be a repaint rather than the true identity; so it is recorded here only as a marking. Whether the airframe is a B or a K (the CIA pair were K models) is unresolved. Confirmed in operation and in place through 2025.
